ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Calamity Jane

code.originalText: Sixteen-week review after a two-day return to drinking: liver tests, PEth, elastography and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Sixteen-week review after a two-day return to drinking. [S]

Ms. Canary returns six weeks after her ten-week review. Her third injection was due four weeks after the second, but she was away for ranch work and it was given four days late. On the two days before it, after a hard week, she drank about half a pint of whiskey each day. On the second day she called the peer recovery specialist, who met her the next morning and brought her to the nurse for the injection. She has had no alcohol in the three weeks since and had no shakes or sweats. She told us about it herself and was afraid we would be angry. Her mammogram at the mobile unit last week was normal. She is eating two or three meals a day. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-22; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 116/74, pulse 72; weight 52.6 kg, BMI 19.3

Alcohol use disorder, severe (nine of eleven DSM-5-TR criteria), daily drinking of about a pint of whiskey with heavier binges for many years; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented lifelong heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding; DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder maps to F10.20 when withdrawal is coded separately. Person-first language; not a claim about her real diagnosis.
Alcohol withdrawal, mild, at low risk of complications (PAWSS 3, CIWA-Ar 9 at intake; no past seizures or delirium tremens), managed as an outpatient with daily nurse checks
S — Synthetic withdrawal episode; resolved by the one-week visit.
Raised liver enzymes (AST 96, ALT 44, GGT 240 U/L) with a FIB-4 index of 3.93, above the cut point for possible advanced fibrosis; liver stiffness measurement planned
S — Synthetic presenting finding; superseded when elastography and the clinical picture supported alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease.
Alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease, without cirrhosis: liver stiffness 9.6 kPa after four weeks without alcohol, falling enzymes, normal bilirubin, albumin, INR and platelets
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the four-week visit.
Depressive symptoms during heavy drinking (PHQ-9 14, item 9 scored 0); whether they are alcohol-induced or an independent depression to be judged after two to four weeks without alcohol
S — Synthetic provisional finding; resolved as the PHQ-9 fell to 5 after ten weeks without alcohol, consistent with alcohol-induced depressive symptoms. Not a claim about her real mood.
Daily chewing tobacco for many years; not ready to stop at intake
S — Synthetic modern coding anchored to the documented chewing tobacco.
Underweight (BMI 18.4) with poor food intake, low folate, magnesium and phosphate, and slightly low albumin
S — Synthetic finding anchored to a contemporary impression of poor nutrition (R).
Housing instability: staying in a spare room at a friend's house, with nowhere to go if that ends; has stayed in shelters in past winters
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and moves from town to town.
Food insecurity: often goes without meals at the end of the month
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty.
Periapical abscess of a lower left molar with facial swelling and low-grade fever, on naltrexone; treated without opioids, tooth removed at the dental clinic the next day; resolved
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Severe alcohol use disorder in early remission, with a brief return to drinking (F10.20). Two days of drinking after twelve weeks without alcohol, ended by her own call for help; PEth 64 ng/mL three weeks later agrees with her account. A return to drinking is common in recovery and is not a failure; she used her plan. The late injection may have contributed. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the rifle remains with her friend. [S]
Continue extended-release naltrexone every four weeks; the next injection booked on a day she chose, with a reminder call and a ride if needed.
Add a second weekly peer contact for a month.
Review her plan for hard weeks with the peer specialist.

Alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (K70.0). Liver stiffness 6.8 kPa, below 8 kPa, so advanced fibrosis is unlikely. AST 31 and ALT 24 U/L are normal; GGT 58 U/L remains mildly raised after the lapse; albumin 3.9 g/dL; platelets 214. FIB-4 1.30. [S]
Liver tests every six months; elastography yearly while she stays well.
Second hepatitis A dose in four months.

list.item: Finish withdrawal safely at home without a seizure or delirium. Outcome by 2026-03-09: Five days of gabapentin with daily nurse checks; CIWA-Ar 9 at intake, 10 at most, 2 at one week; no seizure, hallucinations or confusion [S]

No drinking, her goal, with a medicine for alcohol use disorder. Outcome by 2026-06-22: No alcohol for twelve weeks, then two days of drinking in late May, followed by three weeks without; PEth 820 to 24, then 64 after the lapse [S]
Liver tests back to normal and a clear answer on liver scarring. Outcome by 2026-06-22: AST 96 to 31 and ALT 44 to 24 U/L; liver stiffness 9.6 to 6.8 kPa; no advanced fibrosis [S]
Regular meals and a healthier weight. Outcome by 2026-06-22: Weight 50.0 to 52.6 kg (BMI 18.4 to 19.3); SNAP benefits and two meals a day on most days [S]
A room of her own and health coverage. Outcome by 2026-06-22: Medicaid approved by the four-week visit; a rented room through a housing program by the ten-week visit [S]
PHQ-9 below 10, and reassessment once she has stopped drinking. Outcome by 2026-05-11: PHQ-9 14 to 5 after ten weeks without alcohol [S]
